title: Which machine to play?
objectives: Write a bandit simulator and measure regret against always playing the best arm.

screens.title: Regret
screens.prose: Each order is a pull of an arm $a$ and its fill is the reward $R$, 1 or 0. An arm's **value** is $q(a) = E[R \mid a]$; the best is $q^* = 0.60$. Over $T$ pulls, **regret** is $T q^* - \sum_t E[R_t]$: the fills lost against always playing the best arm.
screens.question: An agent picks a venue uniformly at random for each of 1,000 orders. What is its expected regret? Give a decimal to 2 places.

hints.text: A random pick fills with the average of the three chances.
That average is 0.5333. Regret is $1000 \times (0.60 - 0.5333)$.

feedback.correct: Random play fills $1000 \times \tfrac{1.6}{3} = 533.33$ on average, so regret is $600 - 533.33 = 66.67$.
feedback.generic: Not quite. Work out the average fill chance of a random pick first.

byKey.fills: That is the expected number of fills. Regret is the gap to 600.
byKey.two-arms: You averaged A and B only. A random pick can land on C too.
byKey.per-order: That is the regret per order. Multiply by the 1,000 orders.

explain.text: A random pick has value $(0.45 + 0.55 + 0.60)/3 = 0.5333$. So regret is $1000 \times (0.60 - \tfrac{1.6}{3}) = 66.67$ fills. Any agent worth building must beat this ceiling.

screens.title: Updating an estimate
screens.prose: An agent keeps one estimate $Q$ per arm. It need not store every reward. After the $n$th reward $R_n$ it updates $$Q_{n+1} = Q_n + \tfrac{1}{n}(R_n - Q_n),$$ starting from $Q_1 = 0$. Venue C returns 1, 0, 1, 1.
screens.question: Fill in the error and the new estimate for the fourth reward. Give decimals to 4 places.

hints.text: The error is the reward minus the old estimate.
Here $n = 4$, so the step is $\tfrac14$.
Error $1 - 0.6667 = 0.3333$. New estimate $0.6667 + \tfrac14 \times 0.3333$.

feedback.correct: The error is 0.3333 and the new estimate is $0.6667 + 0.0833 = 0.75$, the plain mean of 1, 0, 1, 1.
feedback.generic: Not quite. Take the error first, then a quarter of it.

byKey.no-error: You wrote the reward itself. The error is the reward minus the old estimate.
byKey.full-step: You added the whole error. The step is $\tfrac{1}{n} = \tfrac14$.
byKey.third: You used a step of $\tfrac13$. This is the fourth reward, so the step is $\tfrac14$.

explain.text: The update adds a quarter of the error: $0.6667 + \tfrac14(1 - 0.6667) = 0.75$. That equals $(1 + 0 + 1 + 1)/4 = 0.75$, so the running mean needs no list. The shape is new estimate = old + step × error.

screens.title: A bandit simulator
screens.prose: Write `pull(p, rng)`: return 1 when `rng.random() < p`, else 0, so a seeded `random.Random` gives the same orders every time. Then write `regret(ps, pulls)`, where `pulls[a]` counts the pulls of arm `a`. Each pull of arm $a$ loses $q^* - q(a)$ on average.
screens.question: Complete `pull` and `regret`.

screens.title: The greedy agent
screens.prose: The greedy agent starts every $Q$ at 0. Each step it picks `a = argmax_random(Q, rng)`, then `r = pull(ps[a], rng)`. It adds 1 to `n[a]` and updates `Q[a]` by old + step × error. Both helpers are written for you; keep that order of random calls.
screens.question: Complete `run_greedy`.

widget.solution:
import random

def pull(p, rng):
    return 1 if rng.random() < p else 0

def argmax_random(values, rng):
    """The index of a largest value; ties are broken at random."""
    best = [i for i, v in enumerate(values) if v == max(values)]
    return rng.choice(best)

def run_greedy(ps, T, seed):
    """Always play the arm with the best estimate. Return (total reward, pulls per arm)."""
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    k = len(ps)
    Q = [0.0] * k
    n = [0] * k
    total = 0
    for _ in range(T):
        a = argmax_random(Q, rng)
        r = pull(ps[a], rng)
        n[a] += 1
        Q[a] += (r - Q[a]) / n[a]   # old + step * error
        total += r
    return total, n

    return 1 if rng.random() < p else 0

    best = [i for i, v in enumerate(values) if v == max(values)]

    rng = random.Random(seed)
    k = len(ps)
    Q = [0.0] * k
    n = [0] * k
    total = 0

        a = Q.index(max(Q))
        r = pull(ps[a], rng)

import random

def pull(p, rng):
    return 1 if rng.random() < p else 0

def argmax_random(values, rng):
    """The index of a largest value; ties are broken at random."""
    best = [i for i, v in enumerate(values) if v == max(values)]
    return rng.choice(best)

def run_greedy(ps, T, seed):
    """Always play the arm with the best estimate. Return (total reward, pulls per arm)."""
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    k = len(ps)
    Q = [0.0] * k
    n = [0] * k
    total = 0
    for _ in range(T):
        a = argmax_random(Q, rng)
        r = pull(ps[a], rng)
        n[a] += 1
        Q[a] += 0.1 * (r - Q[a])   # old + step * error
        total += r
    return total, n
mutants.symptom: Q[a] += 0.1 * (r - Q[a]): not the running mean.

screens.title: A month of routing
screens.prose: Last month the desk sent 6,000 orders. Lit venue L got 2,000 (fill chance 0.58), dark pool D got 3,000 (0.52) and lit venue M got 1,000 (0.61). An unfilled order costs £1.80 of slippage on average.
screens.question: Against sending every order to the best venue, what did the routing cost, in pounds?

hints.text: The best venue is M. Find each venue's gap to 0.61.
L loses 0.03 a pull and D loses 0.09.
Lost fills $2000 \times 0.03 + 3000 \times 0.09 = 330$. Each costs £1.80.

byKey.fills: That is the regret in fills. Each lost fill costs £1.80.
byKey.d-only: You counted only the dark pool. L also trails M, by 0.03 a pull.

explain.text: M is best at 0.61. The routing lost $2000 \times 0.03 + 3000 \times 0.09 = 330$ fills against it. At £1.80 each that is £594.

ideas: A bandit is a set of arms with unknown values $q(a) = E[R \mid a]$. Each pull pays a reward and tells you a little about one arm.
Regret $T q^* - \sum_t E[R_t]$ counts the reward lost against always playing the best arm. From pull counts it is $\sum_a n_a (q^* - q(a))$.
A running mean needs no list: new estimate = old + step × error, with step $\tfrac1n$. A greedy agent can lock onto a worse arm after one lucky pull.
